ὀπάζω: to make to follow, send with
ὀπυίω: to marry, wed, take to wife
ὀργίζω: to make angry, provoke to anger, irritate
ὀροθύνω: to stir up, rouse, urge on, excite
ὀρούω: to rise and rush violently on, to move quickly, rush on, hasten, dart forward
ὀρφανεύω: to take care of, rear orphans
ὀσφραίνομαι: to catch scent of, smell, scent, track
ὀτρύνω: to stir up, rouse, egg on, spur on, encourage
ὀχθέω: to be sorely angered, to be vexed in spirit
ὀχλίζω: to move by a lever, to heave up
ὀχυρόω: to make fast and sure, fortify
ὁδόω: to lead by the right way
ὁμιλέω: to be in company with, consort with
ὁμολογέω: agree, say the same thing as
ὁμονοέω: to be of one mind, agree together, live in harmony
ὁπλίζω: to equip, make ready; to arm
ὁρμίζω: to bring to a safe anchorage, bring into harbour, to moor, anchor
ὄλλυμι: to destroy, make an end of
ὄνομαι: to blame, find fault with, throw a slur upon, treat scornfully
ὑπέρχομαι: to go or come under; creep up, sneak in
ὑπέχω: to hold under, uphold; undergo, suffer, be accountable
ὑπαλείφω: to lay thinly on, to spread like salve
ὑπαλύσκω: to avoid, shun, flee from, escape
ὑπαντάω: to come or go to meet
ὑπαντιάζω: to come or go to meet, encounter
ὑπεξέρχομαι: to go out from under: to go out secretly, withdraw, retire
ὑπερέχω: to hold sth over or above sth; to excel, outdo
ὑπεραίρω: to lift or raise up over; (intr.) to excel, exceed
ὑπερβάλλω: to throw over; outdo, surpass, postpone
ὑπερκαταβαίνω: to get down over, get quite over
ὑπεροπλίζομαι: to vanquish by force of arms
ὑπερφρονέω: to be over-proud, to have high thoughts
ὑπηρετέω: to do service on board ship, to do rower’s service
ὑποβάλλω: throw, put, lay under; bring in as one’s own
ὑπογράφω: to write under an inscription, subjoin
ὑποδέω: to bind under: put shoes on
ὑποζεύγνυμι: to yoke under, put under the yoke
ὑποθορυβέω: to begin to make a clamour
ὑποθωπεύω: to flatter a little, win by flattery
ὑποκάμπτω: to bend short back, turn in under
ὑποκλίνω: bend under, mid. to recline, lie down under
ὑπολαμβάνω: take up; understand, interpret; assume; reply, rejoin
ὑποστρέφω: to turn round about, turn back
ὑποφαίνω: to bring to light from under
ὑφάπτω: to set on fire from underneath
ὑφίστημι: to place under; mid. to submit, to promise
ὑφαιρέω: (lit. to seize underneath), take away, steal, take gradually, deduct
ὑφηγέομαι: to go just before, to guide, lead
ὠδίνω: to be in labor, give birth; to be in pain
ὠθέω: to thrust, push, shove, force onwards
ὠφελέω: to help, aid, assist, to be of use
ῥέπω: to incline downwards, to sink, fall
